401874960.overall: Sassuolo (17th, five straight defeats, 8 points) play their first game under Roberto D'Aversa, who replaced the sacked Aquilani and is expected to switch to a 4-3-3 with a focus on balance. Adzic (knee) and Volpato are out, both counted by the numbers; the good news is Berardi, who has trained with the group and is listed to start in a line-up guide updated Saturday, between Laurienté and Esposito or Bowie, and Muric may return in goal. Genoa (13th, four wins in their last six) under De Rossi have almost the whole squad, with Frendrup doubtful (Wiafe the alternative) and Osmajic expected up front. Referee Maria Sole Ferrieri Caputi has a one-game Serie A record here, which the numbers blend toward the average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already cut heavily for Sassuolo's missing attackers (Adzic -14%, Volpato -4%). Berardi now looks set to start, which the numbers already assume; what they can't see is a first game under a new coach whose first job is to stop a side that has conceded 20 goals in six, so a small lean down to about 2.45.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. A more cautious Sassuolo might defend deeper and give Genoa more, but Genoa have won few corners lately (20 in six) and Berardi and Laurienté on the wings give Sassuolo some width of their own, so the two pull in opposite directions; I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with a referee record of one game that tells little. A first game under a new coach demanding more fight, near the bottom of the table, tends to bring more duels and tactical fouls; a small lean up to about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. D'Aversa's first priority is a more compact side after five straight defeats, and De Rossi's Genoa are also well organised, which points to a slower game with fewer chances than the numbers expect; a small trim to about 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already low for Sassuolo's poor shooting lately (14 on target in six) and for Adzic and Volpato. Berardi's return helps, but it is already in the numbers; the more cautious first-game plan is not, so I trim slightly to about 8.1.

401874989.overall: Milan (5th, 24 points, four wins in five) host Frosinone (7th, 20 points), whose attack has been one of the league's busiest even though they lost 1-0 at Cagliari before the break. Frosinone under Alvini miss top scorer Raimondo (injured) and the suspended Bracaglia, both counted by the numbers; Birligea leads the line with Ghedjemis, Schmidt and Kvernadze behind him and Terzic at left-back. For Milan, Tomori is ruled out with a hamstring injury (not on the numbers' list, back for Cagliari) along with Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze and Saelemaekers, and Pavlovic is still being judged day by day after his kidney problem, so the expected back four is Gila, De Winter, Diawara and Bartesaghi; Maignan is fit after his scare with France and Pulisic, back from the US only on Friday, is listed to start behind Gonçalo Ramos. Referee Luca Pairetto (4.9 cards a game) is already in the numbers; no official lineups were out when this was refreshed an hour before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already cut a lot for Raimondo's absence (-19% on Frosinone's goals) and raised a little for both sides' recent form. Tomori, not on the numbers' list, is out and Pavlovic is short of fitness, so Diawara is expected beside De Winter in a makeshift back line against a fast, direct Frosinone side; Pulisic, back late from the US, is still expected to start, so I keep the mild nudge to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners and already raise Frosinone's side for their big recent corner count (+9%) while trimming Milan's (-4%). Frosinone's wingers Ghedjemis and Kvernadze drive that count and Milan have won few corners lately, both already in the figure, and the match-day news changes nothing in the wide areas, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards and already add Pairetto's strict record (+35%; 4.9 a game over 31 games). It is not a rivalry and no new suspension risk was reported; Frosinone's quick wingers may draw fouls from a reshuffled Milan defence, but not enough to move a figure that already carries a strict referee, so I stay at about 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted heavily for Frosinone's shooting (+24%) and cut for Milan's low recent volume (-6%). Milan's expected attack around Ramos, Pulisic and Moreira is their usual one, and Birligea has been Frosinone's starter for weeks, so the shooting volume should look like recent games; about 33.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, already raised for Frosinone's sharp recent form (+21%). With Tomori out (not counted) and Pavlovic not fully fit, Diawara is expected to start in a reshaped back line, which should give Frosinone's runners cleaner looks; a small nudge to about 11.1.

401875541.overall: Mid-table NEC (11th, 14 points) host leaders PSV (26 points) in the first game after the international break; PSV need a win to stay top, NEC won their last game 3-2 at Utrecht and have beaten PSV in two of the last four meetings. NEC's defence is the story: Perr Schuurs, Bram Nuytinck and Emre Mor are out (the numbers count them), but Philippe Sandler has had a setback and Deveron Fonville came back from Curacao with a knock and is doubtful, which the numbers do not know. PSV came through the break almost fully fit: Sergino Dest is a doubt after leaving the US camp early (NOS, 20 Nov), Paul Wanner is close but not expected to start, Ivan Perisic is back, and Ouaissa, Nagalo, Schouten and Plea are out (mostly counted). Referee Jeroen Manschot's above-average card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already including NEC's hot scoring run (14 in six), a cut for Schuurs, small cuts for Mor, Geiger, Wanner and Plea, and a little for the high-scoring head-to-head. What they can't see is that NEC are also without centre-back Sandler and may lose Fonville, leaving a patched back line against PSV's league-best attack, with Perisic back; I keep +5%, about 4.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with NEC's recent corner surge (+2%) and PSV's quieter spell (-5%) already counted. Dest, one of PSV's main crossers from full-back, is still a doubt, but Kostic and the returning Perisic give width either way and both sides play open, attacking football, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already pushed up about 18% for referee Jeroen Manschot (3.5 cards a game in 51 games). A makeshift NEC defence may have to foul more against PSV's runners, but no suspensions hang over either side and there is no special needle between the clubs, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, with NEC's heavy recent shooting (116 in six, +10%) already counted. Both teams like to attack and PSV's front line is close to full strength, which is what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target, with NEC's sharper recent finishing already in. With Sandler out on top of the counted Schuurs and Nuytinck, and Fonville doubtful, NEC's back line is weaker than the numbers think and PSV should get more clean shots away; a mild +3% to about 11.3.

401875544.overall: Struggling Utrecht (14th, 12 pts) host promoted Cambuur (10th, 15 pts), who went seven unbeaten before a 5-2 home loss to PSV before the break. Utrecht lost their last two league games (Telstar, NEC), have conceded 34 goals in 12 games, and coach Anthony Correia is under heavy pressure with fan banners at the training ground; he says the plan stays but the gaps between the lines must shrink. Jonathans and Ohio are out long term; Correia said today that Engwanda, Paredes and Jensen are back in the group but not yet match-fit, so at most they could come off the bench, while the numbers count them as out. Cambuur's main threat is Utrecht loanee Rafik El Arguioui; they miss Amofa, Visser and Westerhof, Asselman is still unlikely, and Sports Mole expects Jansen in goal. Referee Allard Lindhout (3.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already counting Cambuur's scoring run (16 in six) and Utrecht's leaky defence (15 conceded in six). Correia himself points to the gaps behind his midfield, El Arguioui is in form against his parent club, and Cambuur are expected to use their reserve keeper Jansen, which the numbers give no goal effect; a mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, most of them Utrecht's (6.4). A Utrecht side under pressure at home should push forward while Cambuur sit in and counter, but that is already the shape of the numbers, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for Utrecht's 12 cards in their last six (+10%) and for referee Lindhout's slightly high rate. Fan anger at Utrecht and a scrappy Cambuur side could add some edge, but no suspensions or rivalry point to more, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, with Utrecht expected to take 17.5. Jonathans and Ohio are out long term, and Paredes and Jensen are back in training but not match-fit per Correia, so at most a late cameo; those absences have lasted weeks and are already in Utrecht's recent shot counts, so I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already trimming Utrecht for weaker recent accuracy (-6%) and lifting Cambuur (+8%) on El Arguioui's good run. Today's team news matches what the numbers expected on both sides, apart from Utrecht's three returning attackers who are not match-fit yet, so I stay at 10.4.

401875543.overall: Second-placed Feyenoord (25 pts, one behind PSV) host Excelsior (15th, 11 pts), who have lost five league games in a row, including 9-0 at Twente, and failed to score in their last four. Feyenoord are winless in five in all competitions after a 5-3 loss at Heerenveen, so Giovanni van Bronckhorst needs a response, with a Champions League game against Porto on Tuesday. Anis Hadj Moussa came back from Algeria with an ankle injury and is not expected to start; 17-year-old Jerayno Schaken should take his place on the right in an otherwise unchanged side (Ernst; Read, Watanabe, Marmol, Lopez; Vanhoutte, Targhalline, Zechiel; Schaken, Ferri, Valente). The numbers already count Hadj Moussa, St. Juste and Excelsior's banned Nesto Groen as out. They add a big derby boost for cards, but this is a friendly city derby with a 'Rotterdam Day' and mixed fan sections; referee Robin Hensgens is average.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals, already counting Hadj Moussa's absence (-14% on Feyenoord's goals), St. Juste's, Groen's ban and Excelsior's collapse (22 conceded in six). Two reports today confirm Hadj Moussa is rested for Porto and Schaken starts, exactly what the numbers assume, and Excelsior have not scored in four league games while Feyenoord's defence has leaked in five straight; those pull both ways, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them (6.8) and Excelsior's drop in corners already in the momentum adjustment. Without Hadj Moussa, Feyenoord still have Schaken and Valente wide and full-backs Read and Lopez pushing on, and they will have most of the ball either way, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, and that already includes a +39% derby boost plus referee Robin Hensgens' average record. This is not a hostile derby: the clubs share loan players (Sliti, Plug), Feyenoord have opened the sector barriers and let Excelsior fans sit among home fans for a 'Rotterdam Day', and a game with Feyenoord on the ball brings few home fouls. I trim a little more than yesterday, -8% to about 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 19.2 and Excelsior on just 9.1 after a dismal run (45 shots in six, already counted). Feyenoord need a win and are expected to field their usual side apart from Schaken for Hadj Moussa, despite Porto on Tuesday, which is already the numbers' picture, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots and barely hitting the target themselves (9 in six). Groen is banned and Feyenoord loanee Sliti should play, so Excelsior's threat stays small, as the numbers already assume; I stay at 10.9.

401875546.overall: The Derby of the North at a sold-out Euroborg: Groningen (9th, 15 pts) have one point from their last four league games and went out of the cup to Emmen, while Heerenveen (6th, 21 pts) have won four in a row, including 5-3 against Feyenoord. Coach Dick Lukkien is still recovering from a hip operation, so assistant Casper Goedkoop leads the team with no direct line to Lukkien during the game (OOG TV, FCGfans). Keeper Etienne Vaessen and Hans Hateboer are banned (counted); Goedkoop confirms third-choice Lovro Stubljar will play in goal, and David van der Werff is back in the squad. Heerenveen miss only Hristiyan Petrov (counted). The bans, the derby boost and referee Alex Bos' slightly above-average card rate are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, already counting both sides' scoring runs (17 goals each in their last six), Vaessen's ban (+6% for Heerenveen) and Hateboer's absence. What they can't see is that Groningen go in with third-choice keeper Stubljar (Janse is also out, confirmed by Goedkoop) and without their head coach on the bench, against a confident Heerenveen attack that Goedkoop says is strong on the flanks; a mild +3% to about 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with Groningen's recent drop in corners (22 in six) already counted. Goedkoop wants to disrupt Heerenveen's wing play, and Heerenveen will look to play through the press and counter, which fits the numbers' fairly even split, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a large derby boost (+39%) and Alex Bos' 3.3 cards a game. The rivalry is real and the stadium is sold out, but that is exactly what the derby boost covers, and both sides have been light on cards lately (counted), so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Heerenveen's sharp recent shooting (+8%) counted. Groningen's press leaves space for a quick side like Heerenveen, but that open style is what the numbers have measured all season, and Van der Werff's return only restores Groningen's usual side, so I stay at 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, with Heerenveen's recent accuracy (+7%) and Groningen's dip (-7%) already in. A third-choice keeper affects how many shots go in rather than how many are on target, and Petrov's absence is a small loss for Heerenveen (counted), so I stay at 10.0.

401875539.overall: A relegation-zone game: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts), both only a few points above the drop. Telstar ended a long winless run by beating Utrecht 4-2 and then drew 2-2 at Fortuna; coach Henk Brugge, who worked at PEC for twelve years, sees these as games Telstar must win. Reports on Telstar's team news still conflict: NH Nieuws (19 Nov) says Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes are fit, with Jelani Seedorf hurt in a friendly and Noach Shenkman uncertain, while Sports Mole lists Alders as out and Mendes as doubtful; the numbers count both as out. This is Alex Pastoor's first game in charge of PEC, unbeaten in four; he is keeping his system to himself but says it would be foolish to overturn everything (Voetbalprimeur). Referee Joey Kooij's 3.4 cards a game is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and defender Alders out (+6% for PEC). If NH Nieuws is right that both are fit, that adds a little to Telstar's attack and takes a little off PEC's, about -1% net, but Sports Mole still has them out and Seedorf is hurt, so with reports split and both defences leaky (counted) I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (25 in six) already counted. Pastoor is building on the side he inherited rather than changing everything, and Telstar's wing play through Martha and Brouwer is what they have shown all season, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's slightly busier recent card count. It is a tense six-pointer near the bottom, but that is normal at this end of the table and no bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu. A possible Mendes return adds an option but not a big change in volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. A new coach's first game can be cautious, but Pastoor says he is building on the side that went four unbeaten, so I see no reason to move and stay at 10.6.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, the league's best defence with 12 conceded, unbeaten at home in the league) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, a league-high 40 goals conceded and a league-low 11 scored under the returning coach Jurgen Streppel. Willem II miss captain Justin Hoogma and Amine Lachkar (both counted) plus Thijs Muller, and Goal reports winger Jaden Slory suspended, though the club-area site Tilbo still names him in its expected XI, so that is unclear; Delanghe is expected in goal. Twente are without keeper Lars Unnerstall, Max Bruns and Filip Thorvaldsen (Twenteinsite, Sports Mole); the numbers count only Bruns, but the others have been out for weeks, so recent form already reflects it, and Stav Lemkin may make the squad for the first time in the league. Wout Weghorst (nine goals) leads the line and Van den Brom has no suspensions; referee Serdar Gozubuyuk's high card rate (3.9 a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six (including the 9-0 over Excelsior) and Willem II's 21 conceded. Thorvaldsen is out again but Twente scored freely without him, and Willem II's thin squad (Hoogma, Lachkar, Muller out, Slory possibly banned) is already showing in their form, so I stay at 3.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, already up for Twente's 46 corners in six (+6%) and down for Willem II's low output. Willem II will be pushed back for long spells, which is exactly the one-sided pattern those figures describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with Serdar Gozubuyuk's 3.9 a game (+37%) and Willem II's 12 cards in six already counted. A side defending deep for 90 minutes picks up cards, but that is priced in, and no new flashpoint or ban beyond the uncertain Slory report turned up, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.5 shots, already lifted strongly for Twente's 145 shots in six (+25%) and cut for Willem II's low output. If Slory is banned Willem II have even less going forward, but that is a shot or two at most and Twente's dominance is already priced in, so I stay at 35.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already up for Twente's accuracy (+14%) and down for Willem II's (-9%). Twente's absentees are players they have managed without for weeks and Weghorst should start up front, so I stay at 11.2.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax (25 pts) host ADO Den Haag (17th, 9 pts) in Maurice Steijn's first game back as ADO coach, against the club that sacked him in 2023. Voetbalzone and Soccernet both say Julian Brandt is not fit enough to start; the numbers no longer list him as missing, so they assume him available, which is why I trim slightly. Dolberg (season), Tsygankov and Adingra remain out (counted), while Amrabat and Kehrer are expected to start and Gaaei is fit again. For ADO, Luka Reischl is out; Soccernet also has Alex Pozo out with a groin problem, while ADO fan site Club Achter de Duinen names only Reischl, and keeper Nikiema and Pascal Mulder are fit. Steijn is expected to set ADO up compact; referee Erwin Blank's slightly low card rate is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, with Dolberg's absence taken off (-7% for Ajax) but Brandt counted as available. Two outlets say Brandt will not start, at most a short spell off the bench, and a new coach usually makes a struggling side more compact for his first game, so a small trim to about 3.3; Ajax's 18 goals in six without Brandt (counted) keeps it small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent count and ADO's normal output already counted. Ajax will have most of the ball against a deep ADO block, which the 6.5 home corners already reflect, and Brandt's absence from the start changes little here, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already nudged up for both sides' recent cards and down for Erwin Blank's lighter touch (-5%). Steijn's history with Ajax adds a storyline, but no suspensions or real flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, already up for Ajax's recent volume (+9%) and ADO's (+7%). Amrabat and Kehrer back adds control rather than volume, and a compact ADO may shoot a little less while still conceding plenty of attempts, so these roughly cancel and I stay at 34.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, assuming Brandt is available. With him only a bench option and Ajax's front line of Gloukh, Tolu and Ouazane expected, I shade it slightly to about 10.4.

401875540.overall: Sparta (14th, 12 pts, two points above the relegation zone after a 3-1 defeat at ADO) host AZ (6th, 23 pts), who ended a four-game winless run with a 4-3 comeback at Groningen and play Sparta Prague in the Europa League next. AZ are without Kees Smit (groin, out until the winter break per coach Echteld), Lewis Schouten, Weslley Patati and Jizz Hornkamp, who left Friday's training with a hamstring problem (AZ Alerts); the numbers count Hornkamp and Schouten but not Smit or Patati, who have been out for weeks. Wouter Goes is fit and Valdemar Byskov is back, with Mexx Meerdink (six goals in seven) up front. Sparta start Filip Bednarek in goal for Michael Brouwer (counted) and Lushendry Martes is one booking from a ban. Referee Ingmar Oostrom's slightly above-average card rate is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already taking about 5% off AZ for Hornkamp and 2.5% for Schouten, and adding 6% for Sparta's keeper Brouwer being out (Bednarek starts, as the numbers assume). AZ are also without the creative Smit and Patati, which the numbers don't list, though recent form partly shows it, so a small trim to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, with AZ's low corners conceded and Sparta's normal output already counted. Losing wide man Patati could cut AZ's crossing a little, but Byskov's return and Daal and Oufkir on the flanks offset it, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in six (+8%) and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). Martes is one booking from a ban and may hold back a little, but no suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, with AZ's 93 shots in six counted (+8%). AZ are short of attacking depth with Patati and Smit out on top of Hornkamp, confirmed by AZ Alerts and Sports Mole, and a European trip follows, so I trim slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already lifted a little for AZ's accuracy (+6%). With fewer attacking options for AZ than the numbers assume and Meerdink leading a thinner line, I shade it to about 9.9.

401875542.overall: Go Ahead Eagles (9th, 17 pts, unbeaten at home) host Fortuna Sittard (7th, 20 pts), unbeaten in six league games but with five draws in that run. Fortuna are badly hit: Fortuna-Online (citing Dagblad De Limburger) and Sports Mole both have Michut, Romeny, Zeefuik and Sinkgraven out, Bayram is out long-term and centre-back Guth is back in the squad but not ready to start; the brief lists no Fortuna absences, so the numbers only see this through recent form. Mohamed Ihattaren (four goals, four assists) and Anthony Descotte carry their attack, and coach Danny Buijs confirmed on 18 November he leaves at the end of the season. Go Ahead have Cillessen in goal for Marsman, Waayers and Saathof out (counted), Margaret and Galvez back from international duty and Tengstedt (nine goals) in form, with James, Linthorst and Nauber doubtful. Referee Martijn Vos (4.6 cards a game) is already a large part of the cards number.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Fortuna are without forwards Romeny and Zeefuik and midfielder Michut, none of whom the numbers take off, and have scored only 8 in their last six (partly counted). Guth starting on the bench weakens their defence, which pulls the other way, so I trim to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, already cut a little for Fortuna's low recent count (20 in six). Go Ahead should press and push down the wings as usual at De Adelaarshorst, and Fortuna's absences are already showing in that low count, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards: Martijn Vos's very high card rate (+40%) pushes it up, while Go Ahead's 4 cards in their last six (the league's cleanest side) and Fortuna's low count pull it down, all already counted. Go Ahead want to be harder in duels and to shadow Ihattaren, which could bring a few fouls, but no bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Fortuna's shooting is down recently (64 in six, counted) and they are still missing several first-choice attackers the numbers don't list, with Descotte and Peterson expected up front, so I lean lower to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With Romeny, Zeefuik and Michut out and Ihattaren left to carry the attack, Fortuna should test Cillessen less than the numbers assume; about 9.3.

401875001.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 points, two wins in their last nine league games) host Inter (3rd, 28 points, four wins in five) on Sunday night; Sarri's side won 1-0 at Monza last time but concede too often when opponents overload the flanks, and they also have Conference League games to manage. Atalanta's back line is the big story the numbers can't see: through the week Hien and Kossounou were still in the gym and on individual work and Kristensen was being judged day by day, so Scalvini and Kolasinac are expected in the middle, with Krstovic preferred to Scamacca up front and Raspadori possibly back on the bench (one report). Inter, under Chivu, are expected to start Thuram and Pio Esposito with Lautaro, back in group training after six weeks out, likely only from the bench; Akanji and Zielinski are fit, while Bonny (counted by the numbers) and Stankovic are out. Referee Fabio Maresca (4.8 cards a game) and a lively head-to-head are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already trimming Atalanta a little for recent form and the head-to-head and Inter for Bonny's absence. Atalanta are likely without Hien and Kossounou and possibly Kristensen, which the numbers don't know, and Inter's Thuram-Esposito pair with Lautaro to come on should find room against a stand-in back line; no late news changed that, so a mild lean up to about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already raised for Inter's recent corner count against an Atalanta side that has conceded many. Atalanta's 4-2-3-1 with overlapping full-backs and Inter's wing-backs are their usual way of playing, and a stand-in Atalanta defence is more likely to concede chances than extra corners, so nothing new points either way; about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Maresca's high rate (+27%, 4.8 a game) and a lively head-to-head (+13%). No suspension threat, feud or change of referee has been reported this week, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already lifted 10% for Inter's recent shooting. Atalanta's makeshift centre-backs point up for Inter, but Chivu plans to share minutes between Thuram and Lautaro in a busy month and Lautaro only comes off the bench, so the two roughly cancel; about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Scalvini and Kolasinac expected in the middle and Hien, Kossounou and possibly Kristensen missing, which the numbers don't know, Inter's forwards should get cleaner looks than the numbers assume; a small nudge to about 9.6.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals: Marseille's run of form adds a little, and Bourabaa's absence already takes a big share (about -19%) off Le Mans' goals. corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners, already trimmed for Le Mans winning few corners lately. Le Mans' back five with wing-backs Buades and Calodat and Marseille's narrow attacking trio cutting inside fit that picture, so I stay at 8.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already take about 11% off for Eric Wattellier, who averages 3.5 cards a game. Le Mans have picked up more cards than expected lately, which is also counted; there is no rivalry or special stakes here, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Marseille are at near full strength and Genesio expects to dominate the ball, while Le Mans plan to sit in a block and break with two forwards; that is the picture the numbers already have and no rotation is reported, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already slightly lower for Marseille's recent accuracy. Gouiri has scored in each of his last three league games and Le Mans have no clean sheet this season, and a Le Mans defence possibly without Yohou could concede more clear chances, but the numbers see the form trends and his absence is not confirmed, so I stay at 9.4.

401882803.overall: Getafe (15th, 12 pts, joint-lowest scorers in the league with eight goals) host Atlético Madrid (3rd, 28 pts) on Sunday night; Atlético lost to Bayern and Barcelona before the break, their forwards Julián Álvarez, Sørloth and Jonathan David have only five league goals between them, and they host Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take Lookman, Pubill and the banned Gudelj into account. corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already count Getafe's high recent corner count (38 in six). Getafe play direct and win corners from long balls and crosses, while Atlético lose some width without Lookman, which the numbers count; nothing new points either way, so 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, including about 15% for referee Gil Manzano (5.2 cards a game) on top of both sides' card form. A Madrid-area game against a Bordalás side built on duels is usually heated, but with a strict referee already counted the number reflects that heat, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots, and recent form has already pushed both sides up (+14% Getafe, +8% Atlético). Getafe rely on long balls and stoppages, Gil Manzano's games tend to be stop-start, and Simeone usually controls a game like this away before a Champions League night, possibly with some starters rested; a small trim to about 24.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. Getafe have struggled to create all season and worked on their defence over the break, while Atlético's forwards are short of form and Lookman's absence is already counted; a slight trim to about 7.25.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off David González (about -11% on Burgos' goals). I lean lower, to about 2.0, because Karrikaburu, Burgos' other main scorer, is confirmed out again and the numbers don't know it, and Albacete are short of several attackers; Albacete's scoring run is already in the momentum figures.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, already adding for Burgos' 37 corners in their last six. Burgos will push Albacete back at El Plantío while Albacete, more direct under Etxeberria, have won plenty of corners lately (41 in six); all of that is in the numbers, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards: raised for both sides' recent bookings but cut about 9% for referee Marta Huerta de Aza, who shows 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average. Dadie, Vencedor, Galdames and Álex Rubio are one yellow from a ban, which can make them a little more careful, and the intense game Francisco expects is close to what the momentum figures count, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots, boosted strongly (+23%) for Burgos' 98 shots in their last six. With Karrikaburu and González both out, Burgos lose two of their main shooters and are expected to start Curro and Forés up front, so I trim slightly to about 25.5; Albacete's form with Munir back keeps it from falling further.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Without Karrikaburu as well as González, Burgos' finishing is thinner than the numbers assume, and Etxeberria says Albacete must be more clinical after wasting chances, so I go a little lower, to about 7.7.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points and six straight defeats, and this is Sergio Lobera's home debut after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife; the club is giving season-ticket holders free tickets to fill the ground. Almería lead with 32 points, their best start in the category, with the best defence, and get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty; only Rodrigo Ely and Melamed are out (Melamed is in the numbers). García Pimienta warns that Lobera's Ceuta keep the ball and push both full-backs high, and says anyone who thinks it is easy is wrong; the long bus-and-ferry trip leaves time to recover. Ceuta winger Edgar Sevikyan missed Tenerife on Armenia duty and his status is not reported. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, with Ceuta's share helped by last season's 3-2 home win (+7.5% head-to-head from just two meetings). I lean slightly lower, to about 3.1: Ceuta have scored 10 in 14 and had the ball at Tenerife without real chances, against the league's best defence, now with Luna back.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of corners (+11% momentum). Lobera's possession game with high full-backs fits that pattern, while Pimienta wants his side to compete for the ball rather than sit back, so nothing points away from 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop counters, but that is the same pattern the numbers see, and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding 30% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking a little off theirs. Lobera's side keeps the ball and shoots from range while Almería need few chances; that matches the numbers, so I stay at 31.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I take a little off, to about 10.0: Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball, and Almería's solid defence makes clean shots hard; Almería's own accuracy is already in the numbers.

401875009.overall: Two struggling sides meet on Monday night: Monza (Ivan Juric) are 18th with 7 points after losing four of five, and Fiorentina (Paolo Vanoli) are 15th with 9 points after three games unbeaten. Both have conceded far more than their chances allow, and Monza's Gustavo Varela leads the line as the league's top scorer. Monza have captain Pessina and Ziolkowski back in training and Birindelli and Robinson fully in the group, though one guide still lists Pessina against Colombo; Folorunsho is on a separate programme (counted) and Maye is day to day. Fiorentina miss Pongracic and Parisi (counted); Ndour is expected to start beside Oulai, while Njie, hurt on his Sweden debut, is doubtful with Gnonto ready, and Atta is at most on the bench. Referee Daniele Doveri is one of the most lenient in Serie A (2.7 cards a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending. Both teams are close to full strength beyond the players the numbers count (Pessina and Robinson back for Monza, Ndour for Fiorentina), and Njie's doubt is covered by Gnonto, so I stay at about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count. Monza's wing-back 3-4-2-1 and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 with Mastantuono wide don't point either way beyond what the numbers see, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already cut by 30% for Doveri's lenient record, which I don't size again. This is a relegation scrap in which a Monza win would lift them level with or past Fiorentina, and such games tend to bring more fouls than a usual Doveri match; a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, already raised strongly for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +14% Fiorentina). Returns on both sides (Pessina and Robinson; Ndour) roughly balance Njie's doubt, so I stay at about 28.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent form. Varela is fit for Monza and Pellegrino leads Fiorentina's line as usual, the picture the numbers already have, so about 10.

401879237.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, one win in their last six in all competitions) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban after his appeal failed (counted), Fabio Carvalho may return from a knock (the numbers still count him as out), and captain Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring, not in the numbers' list) are out for weeks after injuries on international duty, with Henry, Furo, Dasilva and Milambo also missing. Keith Andrews calls Callum Wilson the obvious replacement up front, with Schade another option, and Diouf or Lewis-Potter at left-back. David Moyes has a fully fit squad, Jack Grealish back after his disciplinary absence and likely on the bench, and Thierno Barry (10 goals in 13) up front. Brentford have conceded only three league goals at home, Everton have won one of five away, and referee Craig Pawson (3.7 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban and about 4% for Carvalho, who may in fact be back from his knock. They also can't see that Brentford lose two first-choice defenders, Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry and an Everton side with Grealish available again. Brentford's strong home defence (three conceded) and Everton's poor away form keep this mild: about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. The reshuffled Brentford left side (Diouf or Lewis-Potter at left-back for Hickey) changes who supplies the width rather than how much, and Everton's expected 4-2-3-1 is their usual shape, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered for referee Craig Pawson (3.7 a game in his record) and calm past meetings. No Everton player is reported suspended, Everton have no injuries, and there is no needle between the sides beyond a tight table, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson, who scored in all three Carabao Cup games, starts up front and Carvalho may return, while a weakened Brentford back line should let Everton shoot a little more, so the two balance and I stay at 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Wilson leading the line and Everton's Barry facing a reshuffled back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night relegation derby of the Valencian region: Levante (17th, 11 pts, on the survival line after a 0-0 at Celta) host Elche (18th, 10 pts), who lost 2-0 at Betis and have not won an official game in Valencia since 1993; a win lifts Elche out of the drop zone. Luís Castro's Levante have a near-empty injury list and no suspensions, with Manu Sánchez, Ryan, Iván Romero and Bardeli back. Anselmi's Elche miss Marc Aguado, while Houary (in the numbers) is still out and Yago de Santiago and Boayar are doubts; Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back, though Lemar may not start. No referee has been named in the pages I read as of Sunday morning, and the numbers do not flag the derby.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already high for two bottom-four sides, because Levante concede a lot at home and Elche create plenty. Elche get Villar and Lemar back and Anselmi expects an attacking Levante, but Elche keep missing chances and a tense six-pointer can make both careful. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, 4.9 of them Levante's. Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and cross for Fer Niño, which the numbers already see in their 31 corners in six games, while Levante have won fewer than expected lately. Nothing in the team news changes that, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, low because Levante have been booked little lately (11 in six). This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and Anselmi was prickly in his press conference about the pressure; games like that usually bring more fouls and bookings. No referee named yet, so a moderate lean up to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six games). Anselmi expects Levante to attack at home and Elche's possession game keeps the volume high, but a nervy six-pointer could also slow it down. Nothing points clearly either way, so I keep 29.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brugué and Fer Niño, each side's main scorer, are fit, Levante have a near-full squad and Villar's return gives Elche more control, though Anselmi admits their finishing has let them down. I keep 8.9.

401915380.overall: Bodø/Glimt are 25th of 36 with 4 points from 4 games, so this home game on the Aspmyra artificial pitch is close to a must-win for the play-off places; LASK are 16th with 6 points. Bodø won 4-2 at Molde on Friday and lead the Eliteserien, but Håkon Evjen and August Mikkelsen are still out (the numbers count both) and one Turkish preview also lists defender Isak Sjong as injured, which the numbers do not know. No referee is named yet. I lean a bit more clearly higher on goals than before and leave the other stats with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals (2.7 Bodø, 1.1 LASK), already counting LASK's hot scoring run (+2.8%) and the absences of Evjen, Mikkelsen, Bello and Harakaté. Yesterday Andrade was only doubtful; now an MRI shows an ankle ligament injury with no return date, so LASK will very likely face Bodø's strong home attack without their defensive leader, and Bodø may also miss defender Sjong (one report). I raise my nudge from 3% to 5%, to about 4.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners, 5.9 of them for Bodø as the side expected to have the ball, with both teams' recent corner counts (+0.8% and -1.0%) already in. Andrade's absence matters more for goals than for how often the ball goes out wide, and neither side is expected to change its usual style, so I stay at 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already taking off LASK's low recent card count (-6.6%) and Bodø's (-2.1%). No referee is named yet and there is no rivalry here; a LASK side with a reshuffled back line could commit a few more fouls, but that is a normal away-team picture, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots (14.5 Bodø, 12.5 LASK), already trimmed for Bodø's quieter recent shooting (-3.9%). Bodø's must-win situation and four goals at Molde fit a busy home attack, which is what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already counting LASK's sharp recent finishing (+3.9%) and Bodø's slight dip (-2.0%). Andrade's absence is the main new fact and I have put it into goals rather than counting it twice here, so I stay at 10.6.

401915300.overall: Galatasaray are 18th of 36 with 6 points and Aston Villa 6th with 9, so both have plenty at stake: Okan Buruk's side want to climb into the top 24 at home, Villa want a top-8 place. Galatasaray are flying at home, top of the Süper Lig after five straight wins, but their attack is short: Victor Osimhen (knee arthroscopy, top scorer with 9 league goals) is listed out by two previews and at best a bench option per one NTV Spor report, Roland Sallai (back-muscle strain) and Ismail Jakobs (groin) are out, and Rafael Leão is in rehab in Doha. Villa drew 0-0 with Sunderland on Saturday; Matty Cash (concussion), Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana are counted, Victor Lindelöf is ill and doubtful. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals (1.3 Galatasaray, 1.7 Villa) and take off only Leão (-5% on Galatasaray's goals) plus Cash for Villa. Osimhen, Galatasaray's top scorer, is very likely out or only on the bench after knee surgery, and Sallai is out too; Jakobs missing at left-back helps Villa a little, but overall I trim to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already counting Galatasaray's slight rise in corners won (+2.8%) and Villa's dip (-3.3%). Villa had long spells of possession against Sunderland and will push wide, while Galatasaray lose width without Leão and Sallai; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Galatasaray's quieter recent card count (-8.5%) and Villa's slight rise (+3.6%) already in. RAMS Park is loud and hostile, but that is part of the home record the numbers use, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots (12.8 Galatasaray, 13.7 Villa) and do not take the missing forwards off Galatasaray's shots. Without Osimhen and Sallai, young Deniz Gül is expected to lead the line, so Galatasaray lose their main shot-taker; I trim to about 25.5, a little more than yesterday because the numbers no longer count Osimhen at all.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target, already counting Villa's sharper recent finishing (+6.0%) and Galatasaray's slight dip (-0.9%). Osimhen is the forward who turns chances into shots on target, and he is very likely out or only a late option, so I lean lower, to about 9.7.

401915295.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and still top of the Premier League after a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday. Dortmund are 12th on 9 points but went top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 win at Gladbach, unbeaten in ten league games. Arsenal remain without Saka and Zubimendi; the numbers now take about 10% off Arsenal's goals for Saka but do not know about Zubimendi, Raya or Guirassy. No referee has been named, and the numbers otherwise count only recent form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and now already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka's absence, so I no longer size him. What they don't know is that Guirassy, Dortmund's main striker, has missed every game since 4 November and was left out of the squad again at Gladbach, where Fabio Silva led the line. Raya's possible absence would help Dortmund a little, so I trim only slightly, to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3%). Arsenal create corners from sustained pressure and set-piece play even without Saka, and Dortmund defend deep away from home, which is part of both teams' records. Nothing in the news changes that, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already add about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count, while Dortmund's quieter run is counted too (-3%). No referee has been named, and neither side has a ban or a needle in this fixture that the numbers miss. I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11%). Without Guirassy, Dortmund's attack has fewer shots from inside the box, and Arsenal lack Zubimendi's control in midfield as well as Saka out wide. I trim slightly, to about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+3%). Guirassy is Dortmund's most accurate finisher and is unlikely to be fully fit, and Arsenal have looked less incisive while Saka is out. I go a little lower, to about 8.3.

401915296.overall: Como are 4th on 9 points in their first Champions League season and beat Cagliari 2-0 on Saturday, with Fabregas resting Nico Paz and Perrone on the bench for this game. AEK are 29th on 3 points; they won 1-0 at Kalamata on Saturday but lost Honduran midfielder Kervin Arriaga to a broken collarbone (out about two months), and coach Marko Nikolic was sent off for protesting (a domestic matter). AEK's goalscorer that day, Aboubakary Koita, serves the second game of his UEFA ban here, and neither he nor Arriaga is on the numbers' missing list. Como are without Moise Kean for 'a few months' with a bone problem; the numbers list him but take only about 1.5% off for him, and Diao, Addai and Jesus Rodriguez are also out. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and take only a little off Como for Kean and Diao, while riding their 17 goals in six games (+4%). Douvikas is now the only recognised striker, and AEK are missing Koita, their main attacking threat, through his UEFA ban, which the numbers do not count, plus Arriaga in midfield. I go to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, with Como around 5.6 and both sides' small recent dips already in. Como still attack through the wide areas without Kean, and both their goals against Cagliari were headers from crosses, while AEK are likely to sit back. Nothing here changes the count clearly, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already take about 16% off Como for how few cards they have picked up lately. AEK, needing points and missing Koita after his red card against Real Madrid, could play with an edge, but that is a hunch rather than news; Nikolic's red card was in the Greek league and does not affect this game. No referee is named, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots. Without Kean, Como lose a striker who shoots often, and AEK's attack loses Koita, whose shots and goals the numbers still count. I trim to about 24.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Como's sharp recent finishing counted. Kean's and Koita's absences take away much of the box threat on both sides, which the numbers barely see, so I go a little lower, to about 8.8.

401915294.overall: Both sides have 3 points: Feyenoord are 32nd and Porto 26th, and both need wins to reach the top 24. Feyenoord's slump deepened on Saturday with a 3-2 home defeat to Excelsior, Excelsior's first win at De Kuip in 42 years, leaving Giovanni van Bronckhorst under growing pressure. Anis Hadj Moussa missed that game with an ankle injury from Algeria duty; van Bronckhorst hopes he is fit for Tuesday, and St. Juste is out for longer than expected (already counted). Porto won their cup tie at Paredes on penalties without Kiwior, William Gomes and Samu Aghehowa, who were rested by choice, not injured, and are expected to start here; the numbers wrongly treat Gomes as injured and take about 7% off Porto's goals for him. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and take about 7% off Porto because they list William Gomes as injured. Reports say he was only rested for the cup tie and is expected to start, so that cut should not apply. Hadj Moussa's doubt pulls Feyenoord's side down a little, so overall I go slightly higher, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, with Feyenoord's lower recent count already in (-4%). Feyenoord had 71% of the ball and 8 corners against Excelsior, which fits their usual pattern at home, and Porto's wide play is unchanged with Gomes back. I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and already count both sides' calm recent discipline (-6% and -4%). A must-win game for two struggling sides could get scrappy, and van Bronckhorst is under pressure, but that is not hard news, and no referee is named. I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots and already add about 13% to Porto for how many shots Feyenoord have been conceding. Gomes starting adds to Porto's threat while Hadj Moussa's possible absence takes some from Feyenoord, and these roughly cancel out. I stay at 26.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, including a 13% boost for Porto from Feyenoord's poor recent defending. Feyenoord managed only 3 on target from 16 shots against Excelsior, and if Hadj Moussa misses out they lose their most dangerous shooter. I trim to about 9.4.

401915379.overall: Manchester City are 7th on 9 points but drew 1-1 at home to Fulham on Saturday: four Premier League games without a win and nine straight games in all competitions without a clean sheet. Nunes and Khusanov were doubts before that game after injuries at Forest, Guehi had a small issue, and Semenyo is out until about mid-December (already counted).
